findings.claim: The check passes green on a page whose external stylesheet link is render-blocking but written with unquoted attribute values, because ATTR_RE only matches quoted values, so `rel=stylesheet` (or `href=https://…`) is never seen and the tag is skipped as 'not a stylesheet / not external'.
findings.evidence: src/repo_hygiene/eval_adapter.py:834 `ATTR_RE = r"([\w-]+)\s*=\s*(?:"([^"]*)"|'([^']*)')"` and :875-877 `continue` when rel/href are absent. Replacing the fixed link at index.html:10 with `<link rel=stylesheet href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=X">` (valid HTML, the same shorthand the case's own triage note uses: `<link rel=stylesheet>`) → 0 failures; `<link rel="stylesheet" href=https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=X>` → 0 failures; `<link rel=stylesheet href=https://…>` → 0 failures. All three are the exact S3-FONT defect (measured NEVER PAINTED when blackholed) and the case stays green.
findings.repro: python3 -c "import sys,pathlib;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.repo_hygiene import eval_adapter as A;h=(A.ROOT/'src/sec10k/web/static/index.html').read_text();FIX=[l for l in h.splitlines() if 'onload=' in l][0];p=pathlib.Path('<scratch>/unq.html');p.write_text(h.replace(FIX,'<link rel=stylesheet href=https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=X>'));print(A.run_case({'input':{'checks':['external_stylesheets_nonblocking'],'file':str(p)}}))"  → {'passed': True, 'failures': []}
findings.acceptance: ATTR_RE (or the attribute parser) accepts unquoted values; the three mutations above each produce 1 failure; a link with an unquoted blocking `rel=stylesheet href=https://…` is added to evals/fixtures/repo_hygiene/font-link-blocking.html and the -regression case's exact count moves to 3 (watched red at the old parser first).

findings.claim: The onload regex is case-sensitive on the media value and rejects `this.media='ALL'` (CSS media types are case-insensitive, so that page is correctly non-blocking), and `media="not all"` (another standard non-blocking idiom) is reported as render-blocking — both conservative false positives, neither present in index.html.
findings.evidence: src/repo_hygiene/eval_adapter.py:887 `re.search(r"\bmedia\s*=\s*['\"]?(all|screen)\b", onload)` and :881 `NON_SCREEN_MEDIA = ("print", "speech")`; mutation `onload="this.media='ALL'"` → 1 failure 'no onload promoting it'; `media="not all"` + onload → 1 failure 'render-blocking (media='not all')'.
findings.repro: same harness as R1 with those two substitutions on index.html:10
findings.acceptance: Either the docstring names the accepted idiom (print/speech + lowercase all/screen only) as the contract, or the regex gains re.I and `not all` joins NON_SCREEN_MEDIA.
